learning: If line_loss_events on s-bend and slalom fall below 1 and max_error drops below 0.06, the footprint and gain increase worked: keep both and tune base_speed for completion time. If line loss stays at 1 or more with max_error at the limit, hold the geometry and raise kp further (toward 3) or lower base_speed to 0.9. If oval steering_oscillation rises above about 0.4, reduce kp by 0.3 before changing geometry.
notes: Builder's 16 mm footprint geometry with a moderately higher-gain, slower, more damped controller (kp 2.4, kd 0.45, base 1.1). The change is aimed at the s-bend and slalom drift that race 1 left unresolved.
rationale: Race 1 (entityR2A, 302.7) showed the wider ±0.03 m spread fixed the oval (12 of 20 finishes, mean progress 0.93) but not s-bend or slalom. Both still end 40 of 40 trials off_track, with line_loss_events at 1.0 to 1.05 and max_error at the 0.06 m limit (0.0616 and 0.0692). Under the Integrator's decision rule, line loss at 1 or more with max_error at the limit points to controller gain or speed, not sensor coverage. The Builder's proposal changes only the footprint: sensor_size goes from 0.012 to 0.016 at the same positions, so I keep the geometry exactly as proposed and test that change alone. Controller: the 16 mm footprints give the outer sensors more tape overlap, so the readings saturate differently. The weighted-average signal stays on the same scale, so I keep the sensor_weights [-2,-1,0,1,2]. To cut drift on the tight tracks I raise kp from 2.0 to 2.4, which is about 20 percent more steering authority. To damp the extra gain and the oval oscillation (0.33 in race 1), I raise kd from 0.3 to 0.45. I lower base_speed from 1.2 to 1.1, which gives the robot more time to recover. The oval finished in 1.96 s at base 1.2, so there is time margin to finish at 1.1. ki stays at 0 to avoid windup on curves, and line_loss stays 'last_direction', the setting that has been in use. Expected result, to be confirmed by the race: line_loss_events on s-bend and slalom fall below 1 and max_error drops below 0.06. I do not claim this result yet.
